title: fix(ai/gemini): coerce numeric/boolean enum values to strings

commit.messageHeadline: fix(ai/gemini): coerce numeric/boolean enum values to strings
fix(ai/gemini): make enum retyping property-order independent
fix(ai): preserve Gemini enum schema types

- [P1] No code repair is needed; the contributor should supply exact-head real behavior proof before normal maintainer merge gating.

Thanks for the review, `@clawsweeper` — both findings addressed in `70fcdfdc`.

## 1. Property-order regression — fixed

The reviewer bot was right (0.99 confidence, and the failing case reproduces trivially). The initial patch set `cleaned.type = "string"` inline inside the `enum` / `const` case, but for a schema like `{ enum: [1,2,3], type: "integer" }` the trailing generic `cleaned[key] = value` branch would then overwrite `cleaned.type` back to `"integer"` when it reached the `type` key.

**Fix:** track coercion with a `let enumCoercedToString` flag inside the loop, then set `cleaned.type = "string"` **once, after the loop finishes** — so the fix is independent of input property order.

**Reversed-order regression tests added** in `clean-for-gemini.test.ts`:

- `coerces numeric enum with enum-before-type ordering`
- `coerces boolean enum with enum-before-type ordering`
- `coerces numeric const with const-before-type ordering`
- `leaves type untouched when no enum coercion happened` (regression guard: pure `{ type: "integer" }` without enum must stay integer)

## 2. Real behavior proof — before/after

I mirrored the same change into the shipped `dist/openai-responses-shared-*.mjs` on a live install (`2026.7.1-beta.5`) and ran the exact cases the review flagged.

### Before (current main / released 6.11 / beta.5 without this patch)

`cleanSchemaForGemini({ enum: [1, 2, 3], type: "integer" })`:

```
{"type":"integer","enum":[1,2,3]}
```

→ Gemini rejects with:
```
Invalid value at 'tools[X].function_declarations[Y].parameters...enum[0]' (TYPE_STRING), 1
Invalid value at '...enum[1]' (TYPE_STRING), 2
Invalid value at '...enum[2]' (TYPE_STRING), 3
```

`providerRuntimeFailureKind: schema` / `failoverReason: format`. Sub-agent hard-fails and OpenClaw falls back to Claude.

### After (this patch, both orderings, all coercible types)

```
$ node -e 'import { cleanSchemaForGemini } from "@openclaw/ai/internal/openai"; ...'

reversed enum ({ enum: [1,2,3], type: "integer" }):
  {"enum":["1","2","3"],"type":"string"}

reversed const ({ const: 42, type: "integer" }):
  {"enum":["42"],"type":"string"}

forward enum ({ type: "integer", enum: [1,2,3] }):
  {"type":"string","enum":["1","2","3"]}

pure integer ({ type: "integer", description: "count" }):
  {"type":"integer","description":"count"}         ← unchanged, no false retyping
```

Gemini 2.5-flash / 2.5-flash-lite sub-agent invocations that were 100% failing on the same install (webchat dashboard → sub-agent spawn with full tool set) now complete normally end-to-end. Tool arguments come back as strings and are converted back to number/integer/boolean by the existing tool-argument coercion layer at execution time (which the review correctly noted was already in place — the runtime scalar contract is preserved).

## 3. `check-lint` failure — fixed

The previous commit had single-line `if (...) return ...;` inside the two helpers, tripping `eslint(curly)`. Added block braces in the same commit.
